papers.title: Early-onset atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in young adults: Lifestyle, environmental, and psychosocial risk factors.
papers.abstract: Early-onset atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) must be distinguished from cardiovascular risk factors and subclinical vascular abnormalities that may arise at younger ages. This narrative review critically examines lifestyle, environmental, metabolic, psychosocial, and inherited determinants among adolescents (10-19 years), young adults (20-39 years), and selected adults aged 40-54 years who remain within commonly used thresholds for premature events. The 40-54-year band is included selectively to bridge younger-adult prevention with guideline-based adult risk assessment and is not intended to redefine the upper age limit of premature ASCVD. Epidemiological evidence demonstrates a substantial burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD) among people aged 15-39 years; however, evidence of increasing clinically manifest ASCVD is less consistent than evidence of rising obesity, hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, nicotine exposure, and subclinical vascular injury. Established causal drivers, including cumulative exposure to apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins and cigarette smoking, are distinguished from predominantly associative evidence concerning sleep disruption, psychosocial stress, e-cigarette use, and air pollution. Prevention should combine population-level health promotion with age-appropriate clinical risk assessment, including lipid screening and measurement of lipoprotein(a) at least once in adulthood, with additional targeted evaluation for familial hypercholesterolemia, a family history of premature ASCVD, obesity, hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and smoking or vaping. Coronary artery calcium scoring and carotid imaging are not recommended as universal screening tests for asymptomatic young people, although they may refine clinical decisions in carefully selected adults. Digital tools may support engagement but should complement, rather than replace, validated clinical care and public-health measures.
papers.journal: International journal of cardiology. Cardiovascular risk and prevention

papers.title: Beyond Seizure Management in a Developmental Epileptic Encephalopathy: Expanding the SLC6A1 Neurodevelopmental Disorder Phenotype.
papers.abstract: SLC6A1-related neurodevelopmental disorder (SLC6A1-NDD) is emerging as a leading genetic cause of epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and NDD caused by monoallelic loss of function variants in SLC6A1 (solute carrier family 6 member 1) which encodes a gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter (GAT1). Descriptions of SLC6A1-NDD have centered around epilepsy, but caregivers report other features that drive key aspects of the disease burden. This retrospective chart review and prospective natural history study (NHS) aims to highlight the nonseizure clinical features of SLC6A1-NDD. Medical records of individuals with SLC6A1-NDD from University of Texas Southwestern (UTSW) and from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) were reviewed. Participants had a confirmed or strongly suspected pathogenic variant in SLC6A1. Twenty of these individuals were also enrolled in an NHS at UTSW which included standardized scales and caregiver interviews. Sixty-three individuals were included (40 from UTSW, 23 from CHOP) with 31 males. Developmental delay was present in 97%, developmental regression in 41%, and 58% of those had an atypical regression. Of the total cohort, 60% have ASD. Maladaptive behaviors were present in a majority with aggression occurring in 57% of those. Twenty individuals completed standardized scales as part of the NHS at UTSW. The developmental coordination disorder questionnaire (DCDQ) demonstrated that 90% met criteria for probable developmental coordination disorder. Sleep problems were reported in 56%, but when assessed with the sleep disturbance scale for children (SDSC), all NHS participants scored >39, indicating clinically significant sleep problems. Total SDSC score positively correlated with behavior problems. Daily effects from SLC6A1-NDD cannot be described by epilepsy alone. Combining retrospective and prospective NHS data expands phenotypic and genotypic knowledge. We report the highest association with ASD and unusual developmental regression patterns. Maladaptive behaviors are frequent, commonly aggression. DCDQ and SDSC scores correlated with caregiver concerns but also found higher instances of movement and sleep problems, underrecognized by caregivers and providers. Often, odd movements defy categorization between stereotypies, tics, and epileptic movements. GABA homeostasis disruptions are integral to symptom formation but require better understanding.

papers.title: The Use of Cupping (Hijama) Therapy Among Athletes and Its Relationship With Sleep Quality: A Cross-Sectional Study in Palestine.
papers.abstract: Wet cupping, or Hijama, is commonly used by athletes for recovery, yet evidence regarding its relationship with sleep quality remains limited. This study examined cupping use, perceived benefits, adverse effects, and factors associated with self-reported sleep quality among Palestinian athletes. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among Palestinian athletes. Of 754 athletes screened at nine sports clubs and training centers across the West Bank, 470 (62.3%) reported previous wet-cupping use; 468 had sufficient primary-outcome data and were analyzed. Data were collected using a structured paper-based questionnaire incorporating the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Analyses included descriptive statistics, exact and chi-square tests, Spearman correlations, multiple linear regression, and path analysis. Improved mobility (30.8%), reduced muscle cramps (25.6%), enhanced immunity (16.2%), and increased endurance (9.0%) were the most frequently reported intended benefits. Cupping was commonly reported for chronic or recurrent conditions (99.6%), muscle strain (41.5%), and headaches (41.2%). Higher BMI and greater cupping-session frequency were associated with greater perceived cupping benefit (p = 0.010 and p < 0.001, respectively). Reported inflammation was associated with BMI category, gender, and competition level, while mild pain was associated with BMI category and competition level. Lower PSQI scores were associated with higher BMI, greater cupping-session frequency, and greater perceived cupping benefit. In the multivariable model, higher BMI, vitamin use, greater cupping-session frequency, greater perceived benefit, and manual rather than automated suction were independently associated with lower PSQI scores. The model explained 35.2% of the variance in sleep quality. Cupping-related practices and participant characteristics were associated with sleep quality. More frequent sessions, vitamin use, manual suction, higher BMI, and greater perceived benefit were associated with better sleep quality. These findings do not establish causality. Prospective studies are needed before cupping can be recommended to improve sleep or recovery.

papers.title: Nighttime Respiratory Disturbance and Hypoxemia Associated with Impaired Linear Growth in Children with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Although obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) related hypoxia shows stronger associations with multiple complications than respiratory disturbance, its impact on linear growth, a major pediatric concern, remains unclear. This study investigates independent effects of hypoxia and respiratory disturbance on the height of children with OSA. This retrospective, cross-sectional study clinically evaluated children with suspicious OSA from January 2013 to June 2025. Individuals with other sleep disorders, severe neuropsychiatric disorders and physical disorders were excluded. Subjects underwent overnight polysomnography (PSG) and height measurement. OSA was defined as apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥1 event/hour, and those with AHI <1 event/hour served as the non-OSA reference group. AHI and percentage of total sleep time with oxygen saturation < 90% (T90%), were separately used to evaluate the severity of respiratory disturbance (mild, 1≤AHI < 5 events/h; moderate, 5≤AHI < 10 events/h; severe, AHI ≥10 events/h) and hypoxia (T90% quartiles). Height z-scores ≤-1 SD defined subclinical growth impairment. Linear and logistic regression models analyzed the independent associations between AHI and T90% and height and subclinical growth impairment. Nutrition, endocrine disorders, chronic illnesses, and parental height were not collected and adjusted in this study. A total of 2443 children were included (348 children without OSA, 2095 children with OSA). In linear regression models, higher T90% was associated with a lower height z-score in the full sample (B = -0.005, 95% CI: -0.010 to -0.000, P = 0.033) and children with OSA (B = -0.005, 95% CI: -0.010 to -0.000, P = 0.034), whereas AHI was not (full sample: B = -0.003, 95% CI: -0.006 to 0.001, P = 0.111; children with OSA: B = -0.002, 95% CI: -0.005 to 0.002, P = 0.330).Logistic models showed higher odds of subclinical growth impairment in children with moderate (OR = 1.73, 95% CI: 1.05-2.84) or severe OSA (OR = 1.96, 95% CI: 1.19-3.21) and in those in the highest T90% quartile (OR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.30-3.60), compared with children without OSA. These associations remained stable in females and children aged 2-9 years. To our knowledge, this is the first study to show that greater respiratory disturbance and nocturnal hypoxemia are associated with a higher risk of short stature in children with OSA. These findings support routine height assessment in the clinical management of pediatric OSA.

papers.title: Electroencephalography (EEG) and Quantitative EEG for Acute Stroke Triage and Post-Reperfusion Monitoring: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography and quantitative EEG are candidate functional biomarkers that may complement clinical examination and imaging for acute ischemic stroke triage and post-reperfusion monitoring. This review aimed to evaluate the value of electroencephalography (EEG) and quantitative EEG (QEEG) for acute stroke triage and post-reperfusion monitoring. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science on 4 February 2026, with supplementary backward and forward citation tracking. Eligible studies evaluated EEG, QEEG, processed EEG, visual EEG grading, or EEG-derived physiological markers for acute stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA) classification, large-vessel occlusion (LVO)/medium-vessel occlusion (MeVO) detection, lesion-related classification, stroke control/severity classification, or post-endovascular treatment/mechanical thrombectomy (EVT/MT) monitoring. Diagnostic components were interpreted in line with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 and PRISMA for diagnostic test accuracy (PRISMA-DTA) principles. Risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS)-2 for diagnostic/classification evidence and Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS)-oriented criteria for post-EVT/MT monitoring studies. From 4,796 database records, 3,179 unique records were screened, 51 full texts were assessed, and 15 study records were retained: seven diagnostic/classification studies and eight post-EVT/MT monitoring studies. Acute triage evidence suggested candidate value for EEG/QEEG in acute stroke/TIA or LVO/MeVO identification, with promising individual-study signals for slow-to-fast ratios, hemispheric asymmetry/ pairwise-derived brain symmetry index (pdBSI), relative alpha/theta power, and clinical-plus-EEG models. However, devices, settings, target conditions, thresholds, and validation status varied, and no diagnostic domain was poolable. No diagnostic meta-analysis was performed because target conditions, thresholds, reference standards, EEG systems, and intended-use settings were too heterogeneous. Post-EVT/MT monitoring studies suggested candidate value for QEEG slowing/frontal delta alpha ratio (DAR), relative alpha loss, visual EEG grading, Non-Convulsive Status Epilepticus (NCSE) detection, bispectral index (BIS)/near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), and EEG-transcranial Doppler (TCD) neurovascular coupling (NVC) in relation to early neurological deterioration (END), edema, seizure-related complications, infarct growth, or functional outcome. Certainty was very low for diagnostic domains and low for post-EVT/MT monitoring. EEG/QEEG is a promising but still investigational adjunct for acute ischemic stroke triage and post-reperfusion monitoring. Current evidence does not support a universal diagnostic threshold, pooled diagnostic accuracy estimate, or stand-alone clinical implementation. Larger intended-use validation studies with complete diagnostic accuracy reporting and externally validated thresholds are required.

papers.title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations and Their Implications for Personalized Genetic Counseling in 103 Patients With PRRT2 Mutations.
papers.abstract: PRRT2 mutations are associated with a wide spectrum of paroxysmal neurologic disorders. In this study, we analyze clinical and genetic data from a large pediatric cohort to define genotype-phenotype correlations and to provide a basis for individualized genetic counseling. This retrospective study included 103 children with PRRT2 mutations treated at the Children's Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University from August 2018 to August 2023. Detailed clinical data and genetic results were collected and systematically analyzed. Among the 103 children, self-limited familial infantile epilepsy (SeLFIE) was the most common phenotype. A total of 26 different PRRT2 mutations were identified, 93.2% of which were predicted loss-of-function (LOF) mutations. These mutations were highly enriched in the N-terminal cytoplasmic region of the protein, particularly in the proline-rich domain. Predicted LOF mutations accounted for nearly all cases of SeLFIE and infantile convulsions with paroxysmal choreoathetosis. Clinical features, including age of onset, rates of abnormal EEG and brain MRI findings, and treatment response, showed a gradient across the three phenotypic groups, with the most pronounced abnormalities in SeLFIE and the mildest in paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia. Additionally, 12 novel variants were identified. This study confirms that PRRT2-associated disorders are primarily driven by predicted LOF mutations and, using a large cohort, establishes a genotype-phenotype-treatment response continuum model based on residual PRRT2 protein activity. This model provides a critical framework for prognosis assessment and personalized genetic counseling.

papers.title: A case of acute lithium encephalopathy associated with elevated myelin basic protein levels in cerebrospinal fluid.
papers.abstract: Acute lithium intoxication can cause severe central nervous system (CNS) manifestations, sometimes leading to long-term sequelae known as the syndrome of irreversible lithium-effectuated neurotoxicity (SILENT). However, its underlying pathophysiology remains unclear. We report a case of acute lithium encephalopathy presenting with elevated myelin basic protein (MBP) levels in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), offering insights into its pathogenesis. A 50-year-old man with schizophrenia developed coma following acute lithium intoxication. Two days prior to symptom onset, his serum lithium concentration had reached a toxic level of 3.95 mEq/L, prompting immediate drug discontinuation. Electroencephalography (EEG) demonstrated generalized rhythmic delta activity (GRDA) with triphasic morphology, characteristic of lithium encephalopathy, but not fulfilling the criteria for non-convulsive status epilepticus. A lumbar puncture on Day 6 revealed an elevated CSF MBP level of 141 pg/mL (normal, <102 pg/mL) without pleocytosis or an elevated IgG index. Although his serum lithium concentration dropped below 0.1 mEq/L by Day 8, his altered mental status was prolonged. His consciousness gradually improved from Day 10, but neurological deficits including dysarthria, gait instability, and intention tremor persisted until Day 40 before fully resolving. The elevated CSF MBP level suggests that toxic lithium exposure may induce CNS demyelination. While the clinical symptoms were reversible in this patient, such a mechanism may underpin the prolonged or permanent neurological deficits seen in SILENT.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences

papers.title: Stable Overall Volume, Shifting Structure: Nine Years of Paediatric Outpatient Prescribing and Dispensing in Finland, 2017-2025.
papers.abstract: Paediatric outpatient prescribing varies across Europe, and whole-population data spanning the COVID-19 pandemic remain scarce. We characterised trends in dispensation prevalence, age and sex patterns, therapeutic class shifts, and prescriber channels for all children in Finland, 2017-2025. We conducted a nationwide registry-based drug utilisation study of all children under 18 years resident in Finland in 2017-2025, using individual-level data from the Kanta Prescription Centre. Drugs were classified by ATC code. Annual prevalence was the proportion of the year-end resident child population with at least one dispensation; age and sex patterns were modelled with sex-specific quasi-Poisson generalised additive models. Over 2017-2025, 1,324,517 children received 21.1 million dispensations. Mean annual dispensation prevalence was 50.4%, or 45.1% when systemic antibiotics were excluded. Anti-infective dispensing (ATC J) fell from 298 to 237 per 1,000 children and did not return to pre-pandemic levels. Nervous system drug prevalence (ATC N) rose from 107 to 155 per 1,000, driven mainly by adolescents (lisdexamfetamine +709%, sertraline +305%, methylphenidate +207%). Boys predominated to age 13 (boy-to-girl ratio peaking near 1.5); by age 17, girls received roughly 1.7 times as many dispensations as boys. The adolescent gap persisted after excluding hormonal contraceptives, and boys showed the larger relative rise at ages 14-17. The public-sector share of prescriptions fell from 62.1% to 57.9%, with prescribing to children under 6 years shifting from public general practice to private paediatrics. Overall paediatric dispensation volume in Finland was broadly stable across 2017-2025, but the underlying structure changed substantially. Antibiotic stewardship gains held, central nervous system medicine use rose continuously, and the channel mix shifted toward private paediatric care for younger children. If access to private care depends on family resources, this shift may widen inequalities in children's access to prescribed medicines, although socioeconomic factors were not assessed here.

papers.title: Lesser Occipital Neuralgia Secondary to Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) Mask Headgear: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Occipital neuralgia is a well-characterised cause of unilateral head and neck pain arising from irritation of the greater or lesser occipital nerve (LON). External headwear (helmets, goggles, and tight headbands) is a recognised trigger of pericranial pain, formally classified by the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3) as external-compression or external-traction headache. To our knowledge, lesser occipital neuralgia specifically attributed to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) mask headgear has not been previously reported. We report an 81-year-old man referred for a one-year history of right-sided cervicalgia and hemicranial headache, initially presumed to be spondylotic given multilevel cervical degenerative disc-osteophyte disease with severe foraminal stenosis on imaging. Only on closer review of the clinical history did the temporal relationship between symptom onset and initiation of nocturnal CPAP for obstructive sleep apnoea, together with hyperalgesia sharply confined to the territory of the LON and pain reproduced by axial rotation, point away from the presumed spondylotic cause and toward mechanical entrapment of the LON by the mask headgear. Pregabalin, physiotherapy, and mesotherapy directed at the presumed spondylotic/myofascial aetiology produced limited benefit. An ultrasound-guided anaesthetic block of the right LON, performed under aseptic technique, resulted in immediate and complete resolution of pain on cervical rotation, confirming the diagnosis. This case supports a mechanical, device-related aetiology of lesser occipital neuralgia in CPAP users, mediated by repetitive strap-related compression/traction over the nerve's course along the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle, aggravated by cervical rotation, and occurring even in the presence of confounding degenerative cervical spine disease. Clinicians should consider this diagnosis in CPAP users presenting with cervicogenic-type headache, and ultrasound-guided nerve block can serve as both a diagnostic and therapeutic tool.

papers.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy in an autosomal recessive copper metabolism disorder from SLC33A1 mutation.
papers.abstract: SLC33A1 mutation (Huppke-Brendel Syndrome) is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder associated with copper metabolism and characterized by global developmental delay, sensorineural hearing loss, congenital cataract and generalized hypotonia. We report two siblings under 6 years with novel SLC33A1 gene mutation, born from heterozygous parents. The first patient developed early onset drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) secondary to the novel genetic mutation; the second patient did not develop seizures but shared several other phenotypic features of the syndrome, highlighting intrafamilial variation in seizure penetrance. On electroencephalography of the first patient with DRE, independent spike and wave discharges were noted in the temporoparietal region with generalized background slowing. Diffuse electrodecrement with overriding paroxysmal fast activity was correlated with seizure semiology. Neuroimaging revealed generalized cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly, and bilateral chronic subdural collections. We describe a shared genetic mutation in two siblings and highlight their overlapping and distinct clinical features, management challenges, and complications with invasive neuromodulation. These cases expand the differential diagnosis of copper-related metabolic disorders. Variable seizure penetrance in SLC33A1 related disorders could manifest as epileptic phenotypes.

papers.title: Extreme energy expenditure during a 200 km three-day open-water swim: A doubly labeled water case study.
papers.abstract: The upper limits of total energy expenditure (TEE) in humans have primarily been described during single-day ultra-endurance events, or during multistage land-based endurance events across several days. However, little is known about the physiological limits of sustained energy turnover during shorter multi-day, near-continuous exercise events, particularly when performed in an aquatic environment. Prolonged immersion in water imposes substantial thermoregulatory demands due to increased conductive heat loss, which may further elevate metabolic requirements beyond those observed in (cold) land-based events. The 200 km Elfstedentocht swim, completed over approximately three days with minimal sleep and near-continuous swimming, provides a unique opportunity to investigate the upper limits of human energy expenditure during prolonged multi-day exercise in water. In this case study, we therefore assessed TEE in a former Olympic athlete (mass 103 kg, height 2.04 m, age 38 years) during a 200-km swim completed over 3 days using doubly labeled water. TEE was 195 Megajoule (MJ) (46,700 kcals), corresponding to 6.17x basal metabolic rate over the three-day period. This TEE is among the highest TEE reported thus far over similar periods, suggesting that the combined near-continuous exercise and imposed sustained thermoregulatory demands due to conductive heat loss lead to extreme energy expenditure. Notably, the absolute energy expenditure of ∼14,700 kcal per day exceeds previous limits.
papers.journal: Journal of exercise science and fitness

papers.title: Optimizing neurogenic differentiation of dental stem cells: a critical review of induction strategies and functional validation.
papers.abstract: Neurogenesis is highly active during brain development but becomes substantially restricted in adulthood. Therefore, the nervous system shows a limited ability to self-renew succeeding a traumatic incident or neurodegenerative disease. Dental stem cells (DSCs) represent a unique population of mesenchymal stem cells originating from the cranial neural crest. Thus, they have an inherent capacity to differentiate into neurons under proper in vitro cues. However, this ability is limited by low conversion rates and unpredictable target cell types, along with a noticeable lack of standardized differentiation protocols. Therefore, the primary aim of this critical narrative review is to evaluate, categorize, and critique the neurogenic induction strategies for human dental stem cells reported over the last ten years. By analyzing the current literature, differentiation protocols can be broadly categorized into three distinct approaches: growth factors, small molecules, and combination of both. Although the combined strategy shows a promising potential, the focus on structural outcomes and the absence of electrophysiological validation make it hard to determine which protocol truly generates functional neurons. Moreover, in the few protocols that provided differentiation evidence across morphological, molecular, and functional endpoints, the resulting cells displayed only partial functional maturation, indicating that the generation of fully mature neurons remains challenging in vitro. Moving forward, future studies should incorporate patch-clamp electrophysiology as a standard component of functional validation to determine whether differentiated cells acquire genuine neuronal excitability and to strengthen the evidence required for clinical translation.

papers.title: Network-derived symptom architecture and simulated leverage points during radiotherapy for oral cancer.
papers.abstract: To characterize the symptom network among patients with oral cancer undergoing radiotherapy and explore potential symptom leverage points using network-based intervention simulation. Patients with oral cancer undergoing radiotherapy were recruited from a tertiary hospital in China between January and December 2024 and assessed using the M.D. Anderson Symptom Inventory-Head and Neck module. The primary symptom network was estimated from the original 0-10 symptom scores using a regularized Gaussian graphical model. Strength centrality, bridge strength and network stability were assessed. For the simulation analysis, symptom scores were dichotomized as absent or present, and a binary Ising model was estimated. Symptom-specific intervention simulations were implemented through threshold perturbations and repeated 1000 times, with additional sensitivity analyses performed to assess robustness. Among the 508 participants, dry mouth, fatigue, and mouth or throat mucus were the most common symptoms. Four symptom clusters were obtained through factor analysis. Disturbed sleep showed the highest raw strength centrality (1.182), followed by mouth or throat soreness (1.084) and fatigue (1.077), whereas choking exhibited the highest bridge strength in the four-factor symptom network. No statistically significant differences in network structure or global strength were detected across subgroups defined by sex, anatomical site, or treatment modality, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously. In repeated simulations, pain showed the largest mean modeled reduction in the number of symptoms present under the alleviating intervention condition (mean Δ = -0.696), followed closely by mouth or throat soreness (-0.686). Vomiting showed the largest mean modeled increase under the aggravating intervention condition (mean Δ = +0.514) and ranked first in 75.7% of repetitions. Sensitivity analyses showed consistent effect directions and broadly similar overall ranking patterns. The findings identify several symptoms with relatively high network connectivity or greater modeled influence in intervention simulations implemented through symptom-specific threshold perturbations. These simulation results represent changes in the mean modeled number of symptoms present rather than changes in symptom severity and should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than causal or therapeutic effects.

papers.title: Spaceflight human optimization and performance: positioning astronauts in an operational framework to promote health, fitness, and mission readiness.
papers.abstract: Optimizing astronaut mission readiness is a multidisciplinary endeavor that should integrate concepts from aerospace medicine, human performance, sports science, nutrition, and engineering. Situating astronauts within a theoretical framework similar to that of operational athletes, while addressing top human systems capability needs outlined for future missions, may be optimal for promoting sustained health and performance before, during, and after missions to low-Earth orbit, the lunar surface, and Mars. Mission readiness can be optimized by enhancing physiological and behavioral/psychological performance through data-driven and individualized exercise countermeasures, health and performance monitoring, precision nutrition, and rehabilitation strategies. Appropriate and stable space food systems that facilitate adequate provision of nutrients and fluids to prime astronauts for mission-critical tasks and operational demands are needed, though research is needed into potential nutritional considerations that might be useful for future missions. Behavioral readiness programs should emphasize stress inoculation, adaptive decision-making, communication, Earth-independent operation functionality, conflict resolution, leadership, and team-based problem-solving before flight to promote healthy team dynamics in-flight, along with proper society reintegration and uptake of family and occupational roles post-flight. Exercise remains an essential countermeasure during spaceflight, with an emphasis on maximizing fitness before launch to mitigate in-flight declines and on maintaining fitness levels and functionality during flight through high-intensity multimodal exercise. Following return to Earth, rehabilitative programs serve to restore cardiovascular, sensorimotor, and skeletal function, followed by enhancing skill-based performance components through a phase-based training program. Continuous monitoring systems that provide insight into health, performance, sleep, cognitive, nutritional, and recovery status should enable data-driven decision-making on physical readiness across all mission phases. By integrating insight from multiple disciplines, this unifying approach delivers a theoretical framework for sustaining astronaut health and performance during extended-duration missions.

papers.title: Aerospace stressors and brain health in military aviators: a glymphatic-neurovascular framework.
papers.abstract: Military aviation exposes aircrew to interacting physiological and operational stressors that are often studied in isolation. These stressors are experienced by the whole body: pulmonary, cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and immune responses may influence cerebral perfusion, blood-brain barrier function, fatigue, and recovery. Evidence from aviation cohorts, altitude-chamber studies, and adjacent fields suggests that some exposures may converge on neurovascular, blood-brain barrier, perivascular, and inflammatory pathways before overt neurological disease is apparent. This narrative review evaluates the glymphatic system as one potentially important component of that broader injury-and-recovery network, rather than as a sole or established primary mechanism. We synthesize evidence concerning hypobaria and decompression, intermittent hypoxia and hyperoxia, high +Gz, sleep and circadian disruption, operational wakefulness-promoting agents, noise, cosmic ionizing radiation, and context-dependent chemical exposures. Direct human evidence of glymphatic dysfunction in tactical aviators remains absent, and findings from lower-intensity hypobaric exposure and retrospective clinical cohorts are mixed or null. Exposure profiles also differ substantially among fighter, cargo/tanker, helicopter, and remotely piloted aircraft communities. We therefore propose an exposure-resolved research agenda combining longitudinal neuroimaging, circulating biomarkers, electroencephalography, cognitive testing, sleep phenotyping, dosimetry, and controlled single- and combined-stressor experiments. This calibrated glymphatic-neurovascular framework generates testable hypotheses about cumulative brain stress and recovery while preserving alternative explanations involving direct tissue injury, cerebral perfusion, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, systemic and central inflammation, and autonomic regulation.

papers.title: Smartphone addiction and self-esteem among university students: a moderated mediation and latent profile analysis.
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationship between smartphone addiction and self-esteem among university students, with a particular focus on the mediating roles of sleep quality and physical learning engagement and the moderating role of gender. Both variable centered and person centered approaches were employed. In total, 1,130 valid questionnaires were analyzed. The measurement tools included the Mobile Phone Addiction Index (MPAI), the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (SES), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale-Student (UWES-S). Common method bias tests, descriptive analyses, correlation analyses, and gender difference examinations were carried out in SPSS 26.0. A moderated serial mediation model was estimated using the PROCESS macro with bootstrap resampling, and latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted in Mplus 8.3. Smartphone addiction was positively associated with sleep quality (β = 0.066, 95% CI [0.048,0.084], p < 0.001), negatively associated with physical learning engagement (β=-0.107, 95% CI [-0.203,-0.010], p = 0.031), and positively associated with self-esteem (β = 0.072, 95% CI [0.038,0.106], p < 0.001). Sleep quality was positively associated with self-esteem (β = 0.402, 95% CI [0.248,0.557], p < 0.001). Notably, the positive associations involving self-esteem were directionally inconsistent with most prior literature and should be regarded as unexpected and exploratory. The indirect effect through sleep quality was significant for both female students (effect=0.026, 95% CI [0.014,0.042]) and male students (effect=0.018, 95% CI [0.008,0.029]), whereas the indirect effect (effect=0.007, 95% CI [0.002,0.014]) through physical learning engagement and the serial indirect effect (effect=0.002, 95% CI [0.001,0.005]) were significant only among male students. However, none of the indices of moderated mediation was significant. Gender significantly moderated the direct smartphone addiction-self-esteem association (β=-0.055, 95% CI [-0.101,-0.010], p = 0.017). In addition, LPA identified three distinct subgroups characterized by different combinations of sleep quality and physical learning engagement, and these subgroups differed significantly in smartphone addiction and self-esteem. The association between smartphone addiction and self-esteem in university students appears to involve multiple pathways, with sleep quality representing a more stable correlate than physical learning engagement. Gender differences may also be relevant to this association. LPA identified three subgroups based on sleep quality and physical learning engagement that differed significantly in smartphone addiction and self-esteem. These findings provide only preliminary and exploratory evidence for a multifactorial understanding of the association between problematic smartphone use and self-esteem, particularly given the cross-sectional design, modest effect sizes, and the counterintuitive direction of some associations.

papers.title: Micro-recovery dosing in elite sport: an initiative-taking, organization-wide recovery framework.
papers.abstract: Recovery in elite professional sport is now widely understood as a multidimensional process spanning physiological, psychological, cognitive, and social domains, yet recovery models applied in professional clubs and sporting organisations have been slow to reflect this. Most remain reactive and athlete-centred, leaving the full complexity of competitive fatigue inadequately addressed and the equivalent recovery demands on coaching and performance staff entirely unrecognised. No structural framework currently places initiative-taking, calendar-embedded multidimensional recovery as a deliberate component of seasonal planning. Main body. We introduce micro-recovery dosing (MRD): proactively planned, pre-scheduled 36-hour multidimensional recovery periods embedded within the competitive season as a proposed starting point at five to eight instances per year, extending to all members of the high-performance organisation. Drawing on neuromuscular recovery kinetics, autonomic science, sleep architecture research, occupational recovery psychology, and complex systems theory, we construct a convergent theoretical rationale for the proposed parameters and distinguish MRD from related constructs. We present a role-differentiated implementation framework with supporting evidence and a discussion of emerging AI-driven monitoring tools. Conclusions. Taken together, the four-domain convergent rationale and the complex systems perspective provide a theoretically coherent basis for MRD's proposed structure. We argue for a specific organisational transformation: the shift from recovery as an incidental gap between performance demands to an intentionally designed recovery architecture that encompasses athletes and staff alike. The article identifies the active ingredient problem as the central scientific challenge and sets out a structured empirical agenda.

papers.title: Case Report: Orthognathic surgery combined with distraction osteogenesis for severe obstructive sleep apnea secondary to unilateral temporomandibular joint ankylosis.
papers.abstract: This case report evaluates the efficacy of combined orthognathic surgery, distraction osteogenesis, and temporomandibular joint surgery for severe obstructive sleep apnea secondary to temporomandibular joint ankylosis. A 33-year-old female presented with right temporomandibular joint ankylosis, limited mouth opening, mandibular retrusion, facial asymmetry, severe OSA (AHI: 94 events/hour, LSaO2: 66%), and chronic cardiac insufficiency. Treatment included distraction osteogenesis with temporomandibular joint arthroplasty to improve mouth opening, facial symmetry, and airway dimensions, followed by bimaxillary orthognathic surgery (Le Fort I osteotomy and genioplasty) to optimize occlusion, facial esthetics, and airway patency. Outcomes were assessed using cephalometric analysis, airway analysis, and CBCT imaging. Significant improvement in mandibular retrusion (ANB angle) and facial symmetry was achieved. Occlusion, airway parameters (volume, AHI, oxygen saturation), and mouth opening improved over a 24-month treatment period. Vertical distraction osteogenesis via ramus osteotomy simultaneously increased ramus height and provided condylar reconstruction. Concurrent genioplasty contributed to the expansion of the pharyngeal airway and upper airway volume. This case demonstrates that a staged protocol combining orthognathic surgery, temporomandibular joint surgery, and distraction osteogenesis can yield favorable outcomes for severe OSA secondary to temporomandibular joint ankylosis. Validation in larger cohorts with longer follow-up is required.

papers.title: What Happens After They Go Home? Early Patient Challenges After Same-Day Discharge Total Hip Arthroplasty.
papers.abstract: Same-day discharge (SDD) total hip arthroplasty (THA) offers benefits in cost, recovery time, and patient satisfaction. While SDD THA has demonstrated comparable safety and outcomes to inpatient procedures, there is limited literature on the patient experience during the first 24 hours postdischarge. This study explores patients' self-reported challenges in the immediate postoperative period following SDD. A survey was administered to a consecutive sample of 616 THA patients at a single high-volume institution between September 11, 2024, and June 10, 2025. The survey asked patients to identify the most significant challenge or concern encountered within the first 24 hours after discharge. Open-ended responses were categorized by 2 independent reviewers. Where appropriate and when subcategories were clearly identifiable, further breakdown of responses was performed. Any discrepancies were resolved by a third independent reviewer. Analysis of 589 valid responses revealed 6 broad categories of challenges. The most reported challenges were pain (29.7%) and mobility (27.5%). A significant subcategory of mobility issues specifically referenced getting in or out of bed (9.2% of all responses). Other concerns included varying medical symptoms (13.6%), logistical challenges (8.3%) including medication management, sleep issues (6.3%), and mental/emotional challenges (3.2%). No challenges were reported by 11.4% of patients. This study identifies the most common challenges faced by SDD THA patients, with pain and mobility concerns being the most frequently reported issues. These findings highlight the importance of tailored preoperative education and postoperative support to address early recovery difficulties and improve patient outcomes in outpatient THA settings.

papers.title: Detecting EEG index of arousal in sleeping patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome.
papers.abstract: Consciousness is assumed to be defined by two components: awareness and arousal. However, fewer electroencephalographic (EEG) indices have been identified for arousal than for awareness. Since patients clinically diagnosed with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS) show preserved sleep-wake cycles but markedly reduced reproducible behavioral evidence of awareness, their sleep-wake patterns may provide a useful model for examining arousal-related EEG fluctuations. This study recorded nighttime polysomnography in patients with UWS, patients in a minimally conscious state, and healthy controls. The EEG signal showed that spectral slope could index arousal, fluctuating among sleep stages in all three groups. Both spectral entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity indexed awareness, showing a significant difference between conscious and unconscious states. These findings provide fundamental evidence for the two-component hypothesis of consciousness.

papers.title: The impact of digital and E-health literacy on college students' mental health: the chain mediation effect of internet addiction and sleep quality.
papers.abstract: There can be no assurance about the mental health of college students in today's digital information age without their personal digital health literacy. The current academic studies on this mechanism are in their infancy. This paper uses cognitive behavioral theory and stress response theory to build a chain mediation model of internet addiction and sleep quality. The study recruited participants from a pool of 407 college students and provided the students with standard scales, such as the e-HEALS, AMHLAQ, IAT, and ISI-C. The researchers used the SPSS 27.0 software to analyze the data and tested the mediation hypothesis using the Bootstrap method. The findings indicate a positive relationship between digital health literacy and mental health among college students. Additionally, the study found that internet addiction and sleep quality served as mediators. The complete chain was defined as digital health literacy → internet addiction → sleep quality, with the total indirect effect on college mental health measured at 0.6304. The study helped fill an academic void regarding digital health literacy. It demonstrated that internet addiction can be reduced and sleep quality and college students' mental health can be improved. The study has both academic and professional merit. The study aids colleges in the application of digital intervention strategies and the development of mental health literacy among college students.

papers.title: ANGPTL2 and CP define complementary circadian-associated signals in atrial fibrillation: integrative transcriptomics and external validation.
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) develops through the interplay of electrical, structural, inflammatory, and metabolic remodeling. However, the circadian-associated molecular characteristics of the diseased human atrium remain incompletely understood. We integrated differential expression analysis, circadian gene intersection, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and complementary feature selection algorithms in a discovery cohort. The prioritized candidate genes were subsequently validated using an independent atrial dataset, human atrial rhythmicity data, single-nucleus transcriptomics, and experimental evidence derived from human and mouse atrial tissues. We additionally performed cross-cohort drug repurposing screening and exploratory molecular docking. ANGPTL2 and CP were identified as prioritized candidate genes associated with circadian rhythms. Both genes were consistently upregulated in fibrillating atria but exhibited distinct expression profiles: ANGPTL2 demonstrated stronger discriminatory power at the tissue level, whereas CP showed a larger but more heterogeneous expression alteration. Both genes displayed rhythmic expression patterns in human atrial appendage tissue and were predominantly enriched in vascular and stromal cell populations, establishing a link between temporal atrial biology and inflammatory-metabolic remodeling as well as copper-redox remodeling. The upregulation of their transcripts and proteins was further validated across independent human samples and an arrhythmia-prone mouse model. No compound met the prespecified multi-source criteria for cross-cohort drug repurposing. An independent exploratory analysis of clinically used antiarrhythmic drugs identified favorable molecular docking profiles for both target proteins. ANGPTL2 and CP are externally validated circadian rhythm-associated candidate genes for atrial fibrillation (AF), and may yield experimentally testable candidate gene-drug pairs. However, these findings do not establish causal regulation by the circadian clock, direct molecular binding, or clinical therapeutic efficacy.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Reducing cognitive demand fails to mitigate choice overload: Multimodal neural and gaze evidence for effort conservation.
papers.abstract: An overabundance of options can impair decision-making, a phenomenon known as choice overload. Modern platforms use recommendation and filtering tools to mitigate this by lowering cognitive demand, yet whether these strategies actually improve choices remains unclear. We conducted two experiments that manipulated cognitive demand-by presenting high-attractiveness option sets or by providing a shortlist tool-while recording eye-tracking and electroencephalography (EEG) as participants chose from sets of 6-24 options. Reducing demand accelerated decisions but did not improve choice performance as set size increased. Under low-demand conditions, eye-gaze measures revealed narrower visual search and fixation-locked EEG showed shorter event-related potential latencies and weaker occipital alpha suppression, and the three modalities co-varied within individuals, indicating that participants conserved rather than reallocated cognitive effort. These findings demonstrate that simplifying decisions can backfire: when choices feel easier, people disengage rather than optimize, leaving choice overload intact. Effective choice architecture should therefore sustain deliberation, not merely reduce demand.

papers.title: Music performance anxiety, sleep problems, and disordered eating: the role of performance and learning self-efficacy.
papers.abstract: Music students face chronic evaluative stress, increasing their vulnerability to sleep problems and disordered eating. Drawing on transdiagnostic and self-regulation frameworks, this study examined whether music performance anxiety (MPA) is associated with both outcomes and whether music performance and learning self-efficacy moderate these associations. A cross-sectional survey of 260 Chinese music students assessed music performance anxiety, sleep problems, disordered eating, and self-efficacy. Robust maximum likelihood structural equation modeling and Johnson-Neyman analyses were used, controlling body mass index, age, gender, and years of music study. Music performance anxiety correlated with disordered eating (r = .24, p <.001) and sleep problems (r = .21, p <.001). In the structural model, music performance anxiety was positively associated with disordered eating (β = 0.25, p <.01). For sleep problems, music performance self-efficacy showed a negative main effect (β = -0.41, p <.001), whereas the direct effect of music performance anxiety was non-significant (β = 0.04, p >.05). The interaction between music performance anxiety and music performance self-efficacy was negatively associated with sleep problems (β = -0.41, p <.01). Johnson-Neyman analyses showed that music performance anxiety was associated with sleep problems only when music performance self-efficacy was < 3.80 or > 5.55. Music performance anxiety is a transdiagnostic risk factor among music students, directly relating to disordered eating, while its link to sleep problems depends on domain-specific self-efficacy. Interventions may combine anxiety reduction with balanced self-efficacy support to improve recovery under performance pressure.

papers.title: Associations between household chaos and appetitive traits in preschoolers and preadolescents.
papers.abstract: Prior research suggests that household chaos may relate to greater childhood obesity risk, though mechanisms are unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the cross-sectional associations between household chaos and appetitive traits in 92 preschoolers (Study A) and 184 preadolescents (Study B). Parents completed the Confusion, Hubbub, and Order Scale and the Child Eating Behavior Questionnaire. Eating in the absence of hunger (EAH) was assessed in the lab. Data were collected at baseline and at either 6-month (Study A) or 1-year (Study B) follow-up. Associations between household chaos and appetitive traits were examined cross-sectionally using linear mixed-effects models that accounted for repeated observations within children and adjusted for child age, sex, and annual household income. Sensitivity analyses further adjusted for nighttime sleep duration and parenting style in both studies, and the number of children in the household in Study A only. In both cohorts, chaos was positively associated with emotional overeating (preschoolers: standardized beta coefficient β s = 0.18, 95% CI: 0.005, 0.35, p = 0.04; preadolescents: β s = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.07, 0.31, p = 0.003). In preadolescents, more household chaos was associated with higher food responsiveness (β s = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.09, 0.32, p < 0.001) and lower satiety responsiveness (SR, β s = -0.14, 95% CI: -0.25, -0.02, p = 0.03). No associations were found for enjoyment of food, emotional undereating, or EAH. Household chaos was associated with several appetitive traits linked to obesity risk, particularly emotional overeating across both age groups and greater food responsiveness and lower satiety responsiveness in preadolescents. These findings suggest that chaotic home environments may shape children's eating behaviors and represent a potential modifiable target for obesity prevention.

papers.title: REV-ERBs as regulators of circadian rhythm, neuroinflammation, and glial lipid homeostasis in Alzheimer's disease. A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive decline, amyloid-β and tau aggregation, and chronic neuroinflammation, processes that are tightly coupled to circadian and metabolic dysfunction. REV-ERBα (NR1D1) and REV-ERBβ (NR1D2) are ligand-dependent nuclear receptors that function as transcriptional repressors within the core clock and coordinate programs governing lipid metabolism, innate immunity, and redox homeostasis in the brain. In microglia, REV-ERBα restrains NF-κB signaling, complement and inflammasome activation, and lipid droplet accumulation, thereby limiting synaptic engulfment and tauopathy progression, whereas its loss drives a hyper-reactive, neurotoxic state. Astrocytic REV-ERBα exerts context-dependent effects, simultaneously constraining cytokine and nitric oxide production while tuning NAD+ metabolism through an NFIL3-CD38 axis with implications for tau-induced neurodegeneration. Preclinical studies demonstrate that synthetic pan-REV-ERB agonists reduce glial activation, restore NCoR/HDAC3-mediated repression, improve cognitive performance, and partially realign disrupted circadian rhythms in AD models, although current compounds are limited by suboptimal pharmacokinetics and off-target actions. In this narrative review, REV-ERBs are presented as nodal integrators of circadian, metabolic, and neuroimmune pathways in AD and as promising, yet complex, therapeutic targets, highlighting opportunities for brain-penetrant ligands, rational combinations, and chronotherapeutic dosing paradigms.

papers.title: Photoperiod-entrained circadian regulation of downstream transporter networks mediates nyctinastic leaf movement in peanut.
papers.abstract: The nightly closure or downward folding of leaves, a process known as sleep movement or nyctinasty, is a widespread phenomenon in legumes that helps optimize photosynthesis, conserve water, and reduce pathogen susceptibility. Although the physical process has been well characterized, the molecular regulation of nyctinasty remains poorly understood. Here, we combined temporal transcriptome profiling, photoperiod manipulation, and tissue-specific gene expression analysis to dissect the regulatory network in peanut (Arachis hypogaea) during nyctinastic leaf movement. Under normal light/dark cycles, leaves displayed distinct nyctinastic behavior, which was suppressed under continuous light, underscoring the importance of photoperiod for this process. Transcriptome analysis identified conserved light- and circadian-related genes exhibiting rhythmic expression patterns. Key candidates included light-responsive SWEET and aquaporin genes with distinct tissue-specific expression patterns, along with a pulvinus-enriched MYB transcription factor gene. Promoter-binding and reporter assays supported transcriptional links between circadian/light-signaling components and these candidate downstream genes. Together, these findings support a working model in which photoreceptors and the circadian clock coordinate the expression of transporter and regulatory genes, which may contribute to nyctinastic leaf movement in peanut. These findings provide a molecular framework for future functional investigations of nyctinasty in legumes.

papers.title: Benefits of fresh strawberries consumption from Huelva in primary dysmenorrhea: a randomized controlled pilot trial.
papers.abstract: Primary dysmenorrhea (PD) affects a high percentage of women of reproductive age and is one of the most common causes of school and work absenteeism. It significantly reduces quality of life and impairs daily activities. Strawberry consumption has demonstrated benefits in chronic and inflammatory diseases. Therefore, the aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of consuming fresh strawberries from Huelva on menstrual pain in young female university students with primary dysmenorrhea. A randomized clinical trial was conducted including 64 participants with PD, who were randomly assigned to either the control (n = 31) or intervention group (n = 33). The intervention consisted of the daily intake of 250 g of fresh strawberries (Fragaria × ananassa, Fortuna cultivar) for 1 month. The primary outcome was pain intensity assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS). The secondary outcomes included the variables menstrual cycle length, bleeding duration, hours of sleep, absenteeism, perception of health status, State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and mental well-being. The data were collected at baseline, at 1 month and at 2 months. A significant decrease in maximum self-reported menstrual pain was observed at one and 2 months compared with baseline in the intervention group. Regarding menstrual cycle duration, a significant between-group difference was observed between the cycle preceding the study and the second cycle, with a greater shortening in the control group. Perceived health status was also significantly higher in the intervention group at one and 2 months compared with the control group. These findings support the recommendation that healthcare professionals promote the consumption of polyphenol-rich foods, such as strawberries, for the relief of menstrual pain. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06250660 on 2024/01/26. This clinical trial was funded by the Asociación Onubense de Productores y Exportadores de Fresa, Freshuelva.

papers.title: Acute effects of morning versus evening aerobic exercise on nocturnal blood pressure in healthy young men.
papers.abstract: [Purpose] To determine the optimal timing of aerobic exercise for nocturnal blood pressure (BP), this study compared the acute effects of morning and evening moderate-intensity aerobic exercise (65% heart rate reserve, 30 min) on nocturnal BP, and sleep quality. [Participants and Methods] This randomized crossover study included 15 healthy young male participants who randomly completed three experimental trials: (1) morning trial (09:30-10:00), (2) evening trial (17:30-18:00), and (3) a sedentary control trial. The exercise consisted of cycling for 30 min at 65% heart rate reserve. Nocturnal systolic BP (SBP), and sleep efficiency were assessed using the oscillometric method, and actigraphy, respectively. [Results] The morning trial produced a lower nocturnal SBP than both the evening (Cohen's d=0.82) and control trials (Cohen's d=1.23), whereas the evening trial also produced a lower nocturnal SBP than the control trial (Cohen's d=0.32). Sleep efficiency was higher in the morning trial than in both the evening (Cohen's d=5.42) and control trials (Cohen's d=5.12). [Conclusion] Morning aerobic exercise more effectively promoted nocturnal BP dipping among healthy young men than did evening exercise.

papers.title: Distinct brain activation patterns linked to clinical symptoms during hand grasping in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the characteristics of brain functional activation during a hand grasping task in patients with Parkinson's Disease (PD) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and to further explore the clinical factors associated with the level of regional brain activation. Fifty-nine PD patients were enrolled. Demographic data (age, sex, education level) and clinical characteristics (disease duration, Hoehn-Yahr stage, UPDRS-III score, side of onset, motor complications, cognitive function, activities of daily living, non-motor symptoms, and levodopa equivalent daily dose) were collected for all participants. Oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO2) signals from multiple brain regions were acquired using fNIRS during a hand grasping task. With sex, age, and disease duration as covariates, multiple linear regression analysis was used to examine the relationships between clinical variables-including side of onset, constipation, REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), Freezing of Gait (FOG), UPDRS-III, Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), and Hoehn-Yahr stage-and brain activation metrics (both temporal-domain and advanced features). Among the 59 PD patients, 38 (64.4%) had constipation and 17 (28.8%) had freezing of gait (FOG). Under the left-hand task, constipation was significantly positively correlated with parameters in 13 brain regions (pFDR < 0.05), mainly including the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, left frontal eye field, and left premotor area (regression coefficients: 0.0033-0.8538). No other clinical variables showed significant associations. Under the right-hand task, FOG was significantly negatively correlated with the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the right primary motor cortex (β = -8.52, 95% CI: -12.98 to -4.06, pFDR = 0.010). No other clinical variables showed significant associations; however, larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and to evaluate potential subtle effects, particularly for RBD. In PD patients, constipation is associated with cortical hyperactivation in the prefrontal-premotor areas during the non-dominant hand task. Conversely, FOG correlates with reduced hemodynamic persistence and shortened activation duration in the right primary motor cortex (M1) during the dominant hand task. fNIRS can act as an objective tool to explore the cortical mechanisms of motor and non-motor symptoms in PD, providing hypothesis-generating evidence for potential targets that warrant further investigation in future repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) intervention trials.

papers.title: From withdrawal to motivation: The feasibility, acceptability and early clinical benefits of adapted physical activity during inpatient alcohol withdrawal.
papers.abstract: Physical activity (PA) may improve physical and mental health in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet poor adherence limits its clinical impact. Inpatient alcohol withdrawal represents a critical window for initiating health behavior change, although patients are often encouraged to rest. We evaluated whether supervised adapted physical activity (APA) can be feasibly implemented during inpatient withdrawal care and whether it influences short-term health and exercise engagement and motivation compared with free access to a PA room (FPA). In this real-world study, 64 participants with severe AUD (26.5% women; mean age = 45.8 ± 11 years) completed pre- and post-assessments during a three-week inpatient withdrawal program. Participants were sequentially allocated to supervised APA or FPA with general advice. Feasibility (attendance and adverse events), session satisfaction, health outcomes (anxiety, depressive symptoms, self-esteem, craving, sleep quality, and physical functional capacity), and PA motivation (amotivation, extrinsic, and intrinsic motivation) were assessed after acute withdrawal at hospital discharge (post-test). APA participants engaged in significantly more PA (p < 0.05), with high levels of session satisfaction (median = 8.86 and 8.83/10), and an attendance rate of 83%. Health outcomes and amotivation improved over time in both groups (p < 0.001), without group-by-time interaction. Motivation showed a significant group and interaction effect (p < 0.05): APA participants scored higher post-test, while FPA participants decreased in extrinsic motivation (p = 0.013). Intention-to-treat analyses revealed consistent findings. Implementing supervised APA during early withdrawal treatment is feasible and acceptable. While short-term clinical improvements were similar across groups, APA strengthened motivational processes relevant to PA engagement during recovery.

papers.title: Associations between obstructive sleep apnea and Alzheimer's disease-related biomarkers (amyloid-β and tau) in blood and cerebrospinal fluid: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to clarify the relationship between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related biomarkers-specifically amyloid β (Aβ) and tau proteins-in blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) through a systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed, Web of Science (WOS), Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to December 30, 2024 (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251148709). Studies reporting blood or CSF levels of Aβ40, Aβ42, total Aβ (T-Aβ), total tau (T-tau), or phosphorylated tau (P-tau) in patients with OSA vs. non-OSA controls were included. A random-effects model was employed for all meta-analyses. The risk of bias was assessed using appropriate validated tools. Thirteen studies (seven blood, six CSF) were included. In blood, OSA patients showed significantly higher T-Aβ (SMD = 0.66, 95% CI [0.34, 0.97], I 2 = 0%, p < 0.01) and T-tau (SMD = 1.48, 95% CI [0.33, 2.62], I 2 = 93.6%, p = 0.011). No significant differences were found for blood Aβ40, Aβ42, Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio, or P-tau. In CSF, patients with OSA had significantly lower Aβ40 (SMD = -1.13, 95% CI [-1.65, -0.60], I 2 = 0%, p < 0.01) and Aβ42 (SMD = -1.23, 95% CI [-1.84, -0.63], I 2 = 77.3%, p < 0.01), but no differences in Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio, T-tau, or P-tau. High heterogeneity, pre-dominantly cross-sectional designs, low-to-very-low GRADE certainty for most outcomes, retrospective registration, and limited study numbers preclude causal inference and warrant cautious interpretation. This exploratory meta-analysis revealed compartment-specific associations between certain AD-related biomarkers and OSA. However, given the low-to-very-low certainty of the available evidence and the substantial uncertainty reflected by prediction intervals that frequently crossed the null value, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive. Notably, the absence of consistent alterations in P-tau or the CSF Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio argues against a direct signature of established AD neuropathology. Future rigorously designed, large-scale prospective studies are warranted to determine whether these biomarker changes reflect early AD pathology or reversible physiological responses to OSA-related hypoxia and sleep fragmentation.Systematic review registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1148709, identifier CRD420251148709.

papers.title: Associations between perceived stress, sleep quality, and suicidal ideation among Chinese graduating-grade secondary school students: a multi-method study of the moderating role of physical exercise.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the associations among perceived stress, sleep quality, physical exercise, and suicidal ideation among Chinese graduating-grade secondary school students. Specifically, this study examined whether sleep quality mediated the association between perceived stress and suicidal ideation and whether physical exercise moderated these relationships. In addition, machine-learning prediction models and network analysis were applied to identify important predictors and interconnected symptoms associated with suicidal ideation. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among ninth- and twelfth-grade students from 13 secondary schools in Yunnan Province, China. A total of 4,372 valid questionnaires were collected. Participants completed measures of perceived stress, sleep quality, suicidal ideation, and physical exercise. Mediation and moderated mediation analyses were conducted using PROCESS models after adjusting for demographic covariates. Furthermore, ridge regression and gradient boosting tree models were used to predict suicidal ideation, with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) applied to evaluate predictor contributions. Network analysis was conducted to explore central and bridge nodes among study variables. Perceived stress was positively associated with suicidal ideation, and sleep quality partially mediated this association. Physical exercise significantly moderated the direct association between perceived stress and suicidal ideation as well as the association between sleep quality problems and suicidal ideation. Specifically, higher levels of physical exercise weakened the positive relationships between perceived stress, sleep problems, and suicidal ideation. Machine-learning analyses showed that sleep quality problems, perceived stress, physical exercise, and their interaction terms contributed substantially to the prediction of suicidal ideation, with both models achieving an R2 of approximately 0.41 in the hold-out test set. Network analysis further identified subjective sleep quality, sleep latency, sleep disturbances, stress-coping burden, and physical exercise frequency as highly connected nodes within the network. Among Chinese graduating-grade secondary school students, perceived stress, poor sleep quality, and suicidal ideation were closely interconnected, whereas physical exercise appeared to attenuate these risk associations. Integrating stress management, sleep improvement strategies, and regular physical exercise into school-based mental health programs may provide potential approaches for suicide risk prevention among adolescents.

papers.title: Psychosomatic symptom profiles and associated factors of clinically significant anxiety symptoms among breast cancer patients receiving chemotherapy: a multicenter cross-sectional study in China.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy is a cornerstone of breast cancer treatment, but chemotherapy-induced adverse events and psychosocial factors often impair patients' quality of life and diminish its clinical benefit. To summarize the characteristics of psychosomatic symptoms during chemotherapy for breast cancer and identify associated factors for clinically significant anxiety symptoms. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in four hospitals in China. Basic clinical data and medical history were collected for all participants. The 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7) was adopted to evaluate clinically significant anxiety symptoms. The MD Anderson Symptom Inventory (MDASI) and the Symptom Assessment Scale for Breast Cancer Patients Undergoing Chemotherapy were used to collect and assess high-frequency psychosomatic distress. The Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS) measured objective support, subjective support, and utilization of social support, and the Resilience Scale Specific to Cancer (RS-SC) was used to evaluate psychological resilience. Univariate and multivariate binary logistic regression analyses were performed to screen associated factors for clinically significant anxiety symptoms, and Spearman's rank-order correlation was used to explore correlations between high-frequency psychosomatic symptoms and anxiety. A total of 391 breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy were enrolled in this study. The total anxiety incidence was 43.99%, including mild (28.64%), moderate (12.53%), and severe anxiety (2.82%). Binary logistic regression analysis identified clinical stage and cumulative chemotherapy cycles as independent associated factors for anxiety in breast cancer patients during chemotherapy (all P < 0.05). Conversely, age, Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score, and mental resilience were confirmed as factors associated with lower anxiety symptoms for anxiety in this population (all P < 0.05). Spearman's rank correlation analysis revealed that anxiety was positively correlated with difficulty initiating sleep (ρ = 0.358, P < 0.01), fatigue (ρ = 0.322, P < 0.01), and nausea (ρ = 0.366, P < 0.01). Observational findings from this study identify several characteristics associated with clinically significant anxiety among breast cancer patients receiving chemotherapy: younger age, low psychological resilience, poor KPS performance status, advanced clinical stage, and longer cumulative chemotherapy cycles. Difficulty initiating sleep, fatigue, and nausea show correlations with anxiety symptoms in this patient population. These findings highlight that physical symptom assessment and psychological screening should not be separated during clinical care for breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, and provide observational evidence for developing integrated supportive care strategies in real-world oncology practice. https://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2400086704.

papers.title: Adults with congenital heart disease: the growing impact of acquired cardiovascular risk factors on late mortality.
papers.abstract: With improved survival, adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) increasingly face acquired cardiovascular risk factors; however, their impact on late mortality remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the contribution of acquired cardiovascular risk factors to mortality in ACHD. A total of 9826 ACHD patients (mean age 39.0 ± 16.4 years; 50.3% male) who attended our tertiary centre between 2000 and 2024 were retrospectively analysed. Clinical and demographic data were obtained from a prospectively maintained database. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between risk factors and all-cause mortality. During a median follow-up of 10.0 years (98 764 patient-years), 1371 patients died (mortality rate 1.39% per patient-year). In multivariable analysis, older age (hazard ratio [HR] 1.07 per year; P < .001), male sex (HR 1.30; P = .026), greater lesion complexity (HR 2.12; P < .001), coronary artery disease (HR 1.78; P = .005), sleep apnoea (HR 2.22; P < .001), depression (HR 1.45; P = .010), and current smoking (HR 1.67; P < .001) were independently associated with higher mortality, while higher income was associated with lower mortality risk. Both congenital lesion complexity and acquired comorbidities are associated with late mortality in ACHD. These data support the need for comprehensive, multidisciplinary management that incorporates timely modification of general cardiovascular and other risk factors alongside congenital heart disease-specific care.

papers.title: Application of an Open-Source Modular Framework for Pharmacokinetic, Pharmacodynamic, and Safety Simulations to Anti-Tuberculosis Drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) treatment requires long-term multidrug regimens where dosing, efficacy, and safety optimization remain challenging. This tutorial establishes an integrated, open-source, modular framework connecting high-throughput PBPK (HT-PBPK) simulations, mechanistic PBPK models, pharmacodynamic endpoints, and safety predictions for anti-TB drugs. Using the Open Systems Pharmacology Suite and ESQhtpbpk (R package), physicochemical parameters were obtained from literature, with QSAR-predicted values supplementing missing experimental data to generate generic PBPK models. Mechanistic models were parameterized for moxidectin, isoniazid, moxifloxacin, bedaquiline, and rifampicin. A quantitative TB disease model of host-pathogen dynamics and PK-PD interactions was integrated to assess efficacy. A cardiac electrophysiology model incorporating ion channel inhibition data was coupled with PBPK predictions for moxifloxacin and bedaquiline. The HT-PBPK framework automated virtual studies across compounds and dosing regimens. Mechanistic models reproduced systemic and local disposition within two-fold of the observed data. The TB disease model predicted treatment response across exposure scenarios. The cardiac module captured the dose-QTc relationship for moxifloxacin and identified metabolite-driven QTc prolongation with bedaquiline, consistent with clinical observations. This open-source, modular framework spans compound screening, mechanistic PK, efficacy, and cardiotoxicity, providing a reproducible tool to support TB drug development, guide dose selection, and inform regulatory decisions.

papers.title: Global Research Trends in Sleep Quality, Sleep Deprivation and Sleep Promotion Among ICU Patients: A Descriptive and Evaluative Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation and poor sleep quality are critical problems among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, with significant implications for recovery, delirium onset and clinical outcomes. Despite growing scientific interest, no bibliometric study has systematically mapped the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this field. To analyse the bibliometric characteristics and thematic structure of publications on sleep deprivation, sleep promotion and sleep quality in ICU patients indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 1983 and 2026. A descriptive and evaluative bibliometric analysis was conducted. Data were retrieved on April 26, 2026, from the WoS Core Collection using a comprehensive search strategy. Publications were filtered by document type, WoS categories (nursing, critical care medicine, anaesthesiology) and index (SCI-EXPANDED, SSCI, ESCI). Data were analysed using R software with the Biblioshiny interface, and annual publication trends were evaluated using Microsoft Excel. Of 11 418 publications retrieved, 379 met the inclusion criteria, spanning 37 years (1983-2026). Linear regression revealed a statistically significant positive trend in publication output (β = 0.643, R2 = 0.704, r = 0.839, p < 0.001), with mean annual publications of 10.24 ± 8.83 and notable acceleration from the 2000s onwards. Thematic mapping identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation' and 'delirium' as motor themes both highly central and well developed. Emerging concepts included circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain and anxiety. ICU sleep research has grown substantially over four decades, with sleep deprivation and delirium emerging as co-dominant research priorities. Thematic gaps and emerging clusters identified in this analysis highlight important directions for future nursing research and evidence-based practice development in critical care. This bibliometric analysis identified sleep deprivation and delirium as the co-dominant motor themes of ICU sleep research, and intervention-related concepts such as earplugs, eye masks and melatonin as emerging clusters. These evidence-based trends can guide ICU nurses in prioritizing targeted sleep promotion protocols and support policymakers in directing resources toward the most scientifically mature intervention areas in critical care.

papers.title: Reconnecting the disconnected forebrain: multimodal resting-state bold dynamics underlying zolpidem-induced arousal in incomplete Locked-in syndrome.
papers.abstract: Zolpidem paradoxically restores behavioral responsiveness and communication in select patients with severe disorders of consciousness and profound motor deafferentation. While the anterior forebrain mesocircuit hypothesis attributes this awakening to central thalamic disinhibition, macroscopic network dynamics and lower brainstem gating remain under-characterized in locked-in syndrome (LIS). A 45-year-old male with ventral pontine necrosis initially misdiagnosed as vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (VS/UWS) was formally identified with incomplete LIS through systematic ocular testing.
