papers.title: Coblation intracapsular tonsillectomy outcomes in paediatric obstructive sleep disordered breathing: A Singapore study.
papers.abstract: Coblation intracapsular tonsillectomy (ICT) may offer a more favourable post-operative morbidity profile compared with extracapsular tonsillectomy for paediatric obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (oSDB). Data from the Singapore paediatric population remain limited. This study examines the outcomes of coblation ICT in children with oSDB at a tertiary centre in Singapore. This was a single-centre prospective cohort study of 102 consecutive children aged 21 months to 15 years undergoing coblation ICT for oSDB (April-October 2023). Concurrent adenoidectomy was performed in 98.0% of patients. Primary outcomes included complications and disease-specific quality of life (QoL) via the Obstructive Sleep Apnea-18 Quality of Life (OSA-18) questionnaire (where higher scores indicate greater symptom burden and poorer quality of life), assessed pre-operatively and at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included pain, analgesia, diet, and snoring resolution. No post-operative haemorrhage or major complications occurred. All 102 patients completed a 3-month review. The median OSA-18 score improved significantly from 74 (interquartile range [IQR] 54-89) to 29.5 (IQR 23-40) post-operatively (P<0.001), representing a shift from the moderate to the minimal impact band. The mean change of 39.3 points exceeded twice the published minimal clinically important difference (standardised response mean 2.17). Perceived QoL score improved from median 5 (IQR 4-6.6) to 8 (IQR 8-9) (P<0.001). At 3 months, 82.4% had no snoring. Postoperative pain was mild, with 75.5% requiring analgesia for 3 days or fewer. In this uncontrolled single-arm cohort, coblation ICT with concurrent adenoidectomy was associated with low morbidity and clinically meaningful improvements in caregiver-reported outcomes. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant further investigation through multicentre comparative studies with longer follow-up.
papers.journal: Annals of the Academy of Medicine, Singapore

papers.title: Positive interactions and active mentalizing facilitate inter-brain synchronization in couples.
papers.abstract: High-quality interactions rely on socio-cognitive abilities, which help partners understand and respond to one another. Hyperscanning, which measures brain activity in multiple individuals simultaneously, can examine inter-brain synchronization as a possible signature of social coordination. In this study, we explore this synchronization during natural, everyday interactions in romantic couples. Forty-two dyads participated in a naturalistic behavioral paradigm while EEG was recorded. We measured behavioral dyadic reciprocity and negative states, and computed inter-brain synchronization using the circular correlation coefficient (CCorr) across multiple frequency bands (Theta [4-8 Hz], Alpha [8-13 Hz], and Beta [14-31 Hz]). Positive interactions elicited greater dyadic reciprocity and fewer negative states compared to negative interactions. At the neural level, inter-brain synchronization in the beta band was significantly higher during positive compared to negative interactions. Mentalizing compared to counting elicited increased inter-brain synchronization in both alpha and beta bands, indicating that active sociocognitive processing enhances neural alignment between partners. These findings demonstrate that inter-brain dynamics provide a neural signature of both interaction valence and mentalizing engagement during real-world social interactions, putting forward inter-brain synchronization as a sensitive marker of sociocognitive coordination.

papers.title: Determination of the Presence of Daridorexant, a New Hypnotic, in Hair After a Single Exposure and Application to Repetitive Exposures.
papers.abstract: Daridorexant, a new hypnotic used to treat chronic insomnia in adults, has been marketed in France since March 2024. It is an orexin receptor antagonist that blocks orexin binding and promotes sleep without disrupting the natural sleep cycle. Daridorexant could be a good candidate for drug-facilitated crimes; however, to date, this has never been observed in such cases. This study aimed to identify daridorexant in hair. A healthy male volunteer ingested a single 25-mg daridorexant tablet. Two locks of light-brown hair were collected 4 weeks later. After incubation at a basic pH and extraction using an appropriate solvent mixture, daridorexant was analyzed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (TSQ Altis Plus, Thermo Fisher Scientific). In the segment corresponding to the exposure time, daridorexant concentration was 0.029 pg/mg. The other segments were negative. To expand the detectability data for this molecule, a second study was conducted after repeated consumption of 25 mg daridorexant over 6 days. The results obtained are consistent with the findings of the first study, with a response at 0.8 pg/mg in the segment of interest. Furthermore, hair analysis of an assault victim revealed the presence of daridorexant at 35 pg/mg. In this case, the victim voluntarily consumed the prescribed daridorexant for 2 months after the assault to aid sleep. The authors report, for the first time, quantitative data on daridorexant detection in hair after single and repeated exposures. The test results are difficult to interpret because they represent the first data available in the literature. Nevertheless, the use of a sensitive analytical system, such as liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, seems necessary given the very low concentrations measured.

papers.title: Evoked alpha oscillatory activity is suppressed by prolonged elbow pain and modulated by repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation.
papers.abstract: Alpha-band oscillatory activity, assessed using electroencephalography (EEG), is among the most widely studied neurophysiological markers of pain. However, the literature has focused predominantly on resting-state measures, leaving unclear whether pain also alters evoked alpha-band dynamics, measured via cortical perturbation using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). Here, we examined whether prolonged pain alters TMS-evoked alpha event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP) and intertrial coherence (ITC), reflecting cortical reactivity and phase consistency, and whether 10-Hz repetitive TMS (rTMS) modulates these responses. We performed a secondary analysis on 2 previous experiments, which used nerve growth factor (NGF) injection to induce prolonged elbow muscle pain. In experiment 1, participants underwent primary motor cortex (M1) TMS-EEG at baseline (day 0) pre-NGF injection and day 2 (peak pain) and day 7 (pain resolution) post-injection. In experiment 2, M1-TMS-EEG was assessed on day 0 before NGF injection and again on day 4 after injection, with active or sham 10-Hz rTMS delivered to M1 between these assessments. In experiment 1, M1 TMS-EEG showed reductions in alpha ERSP (P = 0.014) and alpha ITC (P = 0.041) from day 0 to day 2. In experiment 2, active rTMS produced a more positive pre-to-post change in alpha ERSP (P = 0.006) relative to sham but did not alter alpha ITC (P = 0.804). Our findings suggest that prolonged experimental pain is associated with diminished evoked alpha oscillatory activity, whereas high-frequency rTMS modulates this activity in the positive direction. These findings suggest that perturbation-evoked alpha metrics warrant further investigation as candidate biomarkers of pain state and response to neuromodulation.

papers.title: Vanillin alleviates circadian disruption-induced cognitive impairment: involvement of gut microbiota alterations and tryptophan metabolism.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruption (CD) is an important risk factor for cognitive impairment and neurodegenerative diseases, potentially through disturbances in tryptophan (TRP) metabolism. This study investigated the protective effects of orally administered vanillin in a mouse model of CD. CD impaired spatial learning and recognition memory, whereas vanillin improved cognitive performance and corrected abnormal changes in TRP-related metabolites, including tryptophan, kynurenine (KYN), and kynurenic acid (KYNA). Vanillin also modulated the composition and diversity of the gut microbiota, enhanced intestinal barrier function, and improved immune homeostasis. Immunofluorescence staining and western blot analysis further showed that vanillin regulated hippocampal proteins associated with neuronal and synaptic function and reduced astrocyte activation. These findings suggest that vanillin alleviates CD-induced cognitive impairment, accompanied by alterations in gut microbiota composition, TRP-kynurenine metabolism, intestinal barrier function, and neuroinflammatory responses.

papers.title: [One anastomosis mini gastric bypass in patients with severe obesity].
papers.abstract: To evaluate the results of one anastomosis mini-gastric bypass in surgical treatment of severe obesity. This study presents the results of a 3-year follow-up of 17 patients who underwent mini-gastric bypass surgery. Their age ranged from 27 to 60 years (median 47.0). Preoperative BMI was 64.28 kg/m² (range 60.0-83.66). The follow-up examinations were conducted at 1 week, 3, 6, 12, 24 and 36 months after surgery. We assessed anthropometric data (BMI, excess weight loss - EWL, total weight loss - TWL), glycose metabolism parameters, lipid profile, blood pressure and therapy. Preoperative body weight was 186.1 kg [159; 230], TWL - 37.6 kg [23; 67], EWL - 57.3 kg [36; 90]. According to our study, remission of diabetes occurred in 84% of cases, sleep apnea symptoms regressed in 94.1% of cases. Normal blood pressure or reduced need for medications was achieved in 50% of cases. Normalization of low-density lipoproteins or statin dose reduction occurred in 79% of cases. Thus, mini-gastric bypass is a relatively safe procedure with minimal rate of early postoperative complications.

papers.title: Sleep-disordered breathing in children with class II and large overjet treated with removable functional appliance - A longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) was examined in children aged 9-14 years with class II and large overjet ≥ 6 mm (study group) before (T0), during (T1) and after treatment (T2) with a removable functional appliance, compared to a control group. At T0, the study group included 37 children, and the control group included 32 children. For both groups, exclusion criteria were as follows: diseases, syndromes, allergies, asthma, mouth breathing, adenoid vegetations, and hypertrophied tonsils. SDB was assessed and scored manually by respiratory polygraphy. SDB parameters between the groups were compared using a general linear model adjusted for sex, treatment time, and body mass index. No significant difference in SDB was found between the groups (p = .258), although at T0, 8.6% of the children in the study group and none in the control group had SDB. None were diagnosed with SDB at T1 or T2. No significant differences in changes in SDB parameters between the groups were observed from T0-T1, T1-T2, or T0-T2. At T0, 8.6% of study group children had SDB but none at T1 or T2. No significant difference in changes in SDB parameters over time was found between the groups. NCT04964830.

papers.title: Mental health and somatic symptom reductions during Ukraine's counteroffensive in the fall of 2023.
papers.abstract: Background: As the war in Ukraine has become protracted, civilians have been forced to adapt to chronic danger, uncertainty, and repeated military threat. This prospective study examined mental health symptom change during a pivotal six-month period in 2023, encompassing the high hopes surrounding the rise of the Ukrainian counteroffensive and the subsequent disappointment of its stall.Methods: We conducted a two-wave online longitudinal study of 208 Ukrainian civilian adults (80.8% female; mean age 29.4 years) assessed in June 2023 and November 2023. Primary outcomes were generalised anxiety, depression, and somatic symptoms. We further examined whether symptom change was associated with baseline sleep disturbance, trait resilience, and sociodemographic factors. Subjective threat perception, confidence in military success, and objective indicators of military threat were included as contextual variables.Results: Confidence in military success declined significantly across the two waves, while objective indicators of military threat, including artillery attacks and air raid alarms, increased. Subjective threat perception remained stable. Despite this unfavourable context, generalised anxiety, depression, and somatic symptoms decreased on average over time. Individual differences in symptom change were partly associated with baseline characteristics. Higher baseline sleep disturbance predicted smaller reductions in anxiety and depression. Female sex was associated with smaller reduction in depression, and older age with greater reduction in anxiety. Trait resilience and socioeconomic factors were not significantly associated with symptom change.Conclusion: The findings suggest that anxiety, depression, and somatic symptoms may decrease over time even under worsening objective wartime conditions. This pattern is more consistent with partial adaptation under chronic threat than with improvement in external circumstances. Sleep disturbance emerged as a robust predictor of less favourable symptom change, highlighting sleep as a potentially important target for mental health support under prolonged war-related stress.

papers.title: Differences of physical activity, sleep quality and depressive symptoms in patients with diabetes and non-diabetes undergoing maintenance hemodialysis in Xi'an, China: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To compare the physical activity, sleep quality and depressive symptoms between patients with diabetes and non-diabetes undergoing maintenance hemodialysis, and identify associated influencing factors. A descriptive cross-sectional design was adopted. Maintenance hemodialysis patients were enrolled from two hemodialysis centers in Xi'an, China between April and May 2022. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected, with physical activity assessed via Human Activity Profile, sleep quality via Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and depressive symptoms via Beck Depression Inventory-II. Of 286 participants, 113 had diabetes and 173 did not. Diabetic patients had lower adjusted activity scores (40.07 ± 22.94 vs. 55.94 ± 21.35, P < 0.01), higher PSQI global scores (9.04 ± 4.48 vs. 7.15 ± 4.47, P < 0.01), and higher BDI-II scores (17.32 ± 10.75 vs. 12.95 ± 9.26, P < 0.01) than non-diabetic patients. Multivariate logistic regression showed that age (OR = 1.02, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.04) and BDI-II score (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.07) were positively associated with diabetes, whereas AAS (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97, 0.99) and MHD duration (OR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.98, 1.00) were negatively associated. Diabetic patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis exhibit poorer physical activity levels, sleep quality, and depressive symptoms compared with non-diabetic counterparts. Accordingly, routine combined screening of physical activity, sleep disturbance and depressive symptoms should be embedded into daily dialysis nursing.

papers.title: A serum cytokine-derived integrated inflammatory profile score (IIPS) links systemic inflammation to symptom burden and severity in COPD.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory syndrome in which forced expiratory volume in 1 s expressed as a percentage of predicted value (FEV1% predicted) may dissociate from patient-reported symptom burden. This study evaluated an Integrated Inflammatory Profile Score (IIPS) as a potential biological correlate for a more holistic assessment of stable COPD. Serum concentrations of 11 cytokines were measured in 62 patients with stable COPD. The IIPS was derived using automated linear modeling with forward stepwise selection guided by the corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc). Associations of the IIPS with COPD Assessment Test (CAT) scores were compared with those of FEV1% predicted. The optimized IIPS, comprising interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), interleukin-2 (IL-2), and interleukin-10 (IL-10), was significantly associated with FEV1% predicted (R2 = 0.1867, p = 0.0005) and outperformed the individual cytokines in discriminating spirometric severity (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.7381). For symptom burden, FEV1% predicted showed greater explanatory power for exertional domains, particularly breathlessness (R2 = 0.0832) and activities (R2 = 0.1280). By contrast, the IIPS showed numerically stronger trend-level associations for sleep (R2 = 0.0519, p = 0.0750) and energy (R2 = 0.0511, p = 0.0773), although these associations did not reach conventional statistical significance. The IIPS reflects Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)-defined physiological severity more effectively than any single cytokine measured in this study. Its associations with patient-reported systemic symptoms were modest and exploratory, suggesting that integrated inflammatory profiling may complement spirometry in characterizing COPD burden but requires external and longitudinal validation before clinical application.

papers.title: Effect of a wearable-based individualised multidomain lifestyle intervention on cognitive and physical function in older adults at risk of decline (INSPIOR): a single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Multidomain lifestyle programmes are the leading preventive approach to cognitive decline, but they rely on intensive face-to-face delivery that is hard to scale. We assessed whether an automated, wearable-based multidomain programme of activity, sleep, and optional nutrition prompts changed cognitive and physical function in at-risk older adults. INSPIOR was a 6-month, single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial in Kashiwa, Japan. Adults aged 65-92 years with low body-mass index, pre-frailty, frailty, or sarcopenia-related decline were randomly assigned 1:1, in permuted blocks of four and without stratification, to the Fitbit-based intervention or an assessment-only control; allocation was not concealed and outcome assessors were not masked. Co-primary outcomes were the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Trail Making Test (TMT), and skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), with no pre-specified hierarchy or multiplicity adjustment; analyses used intention-to-treat analysis of covariance with multiple imputation. This trial was registered with UMIN-CTR, UMIN000052707, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06135740. Between Nov 8, 2023, and Jul 31, 2024, 355 participants were randomly assigned to the intervention group (n = 178) or control group (n = 177); all were analysed. Adjusted between-group differences were 0·58 MoCA points (95% CI 0·03-1·13; p = 0·039; Holm-adjusted p = 0·12), 0·16 s (-5·07 to 5·40; p = 0·95) for TMT-A, 5·59 s (-3·88 to 15·05; p = 0·25) for TMT-B, and -0·01 kg/m2 (-0·09 to 0·07; p = 0·88) for SMI. Mild skin irritation and dietary-recording stress occurred; no serious adverse event was intervention-related. The intervention was associated with a small difference in a global cognitive screening score that did not survive multiplicity adjustment and is of uncertain clinical significance; the other two showed none. Larger, longer, masked trials are needed. University of Tokyo-NH Foods Collaborative Research Programme, Google, Mitsui Fudosan.

papers.title: Isolated Aphasia as an Epileptic Manifestation of Neurosarcoidosis: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Acute aphasia requires urgent evaluation for stroke, but recurrent and stereotyped language disturbances may also reflect focal seizures. We report the case of a 23-year-old man brought to the emergency department (ED) with aphasia that had been present for approximately six hours. Over the preceding week, he had experienced several similar but briefer episodes that had resolved spontaneously. He was concurrently undergoing investigation at another institution for persistent hiccups and near-daily vomiting of more than one month's duration. Chest computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography had already shown mediastinal and mesenteric lymphadenopathy suggestive of sarcoidosis, although other etiologies, including malignancy, could not be excluded. Neurological examination was limited by the language disturbance but showed no obvious motor deficit. Brain computed tomography revealed obstructive hydrocephalus with transependymal cerebrospinal fluid flow and multiple enhancing nodular lesions, predominantly in and around the ventricular system. Electroencephalography demonstrated epileptiform activity, and the aphasia resolved after treatment with levetiracetam and clobazam. Further cerebrospinal fluid analysis, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and pathological investigations supported a diagnosis of probable neurosarcoidosis presenting with lymphocytic meningoencephalitis and obstructive hydrocephalus. This case illustrates an unusual pathophysiological sequence, isolated aphasia as a focal epileptic manifestation of neurosarcoidosis, and is a reminder that unexplained focal neurological symptoms, particularly when fluctuating or recurrent, warrant the consideration of seizures and early electroencephalography.

papers.title: Oxytocin preserves excitatory responsiveness of VTA dopaminergic neurons in PTSD model rats.
papers.abstract: Dysfunction of the ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopaminergic circuits is strongly implicated in the pathological progression of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Oxytocin (OXT) exerts robust stress-buffering effects, yet its direct neuromodulatory influence on VTA dopaminergic neurons under PTSD pathological conditions remains poorly defined. Here, we performed in vivo extracellular recordings to quantify spontaneous firing and burst activity in normal control and single prolonged stress (SPS)-induced PTSD model rats. Graded intracerebroventricular OXT infusions and OXTR antagonist pretreatment were used to characterize OXT-mediated neuronal modulation. Baseline spontaneous firing and burst rates were markedly suppressed in PTSD model rats; however, OXT elevated neuronal excitability in both cohorts, an effect nearly abolished by pretreatment with the selective OXTR antagonist L-371,257. Although absolute firing values remained persistently lower in PTSD model rats at baseline and following OXT administration, the relative fold increase in response to OXT was comparable to that observed in normal controls. These electrophysiological findings demonstrate that PTSD-like traumatic stress depresses baseline VTA dopaminergic activity, whereas the excitatory responsiveness of VTA dopaminergic neurons to exogenous OXT is largely preserved in PTSD model animals.

papers.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Pain Chronification: Neuroimmune Rationale, Evidence Boundaries, and Trial Design Priorities: A Structured Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Pain chronification is a dynamic transition in which persistent pain may be shaped by interacting nociceptive, peripheral, spinal, supraspinal, neuroimmune, endocrine and cognitive-affective processes. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) has clinical value in chronic pain, but claims about glial modulation and disease modification require careful qualification. To evaluate CBT as an early, mechanism-informed and hypothesis-generating intervention while distinguishing clinical efficacy, neuroimmune plausibility, prevention hypotheses and disease-modifying claims. We conducted a structured narrative review using prespecified evidence domains. PubMed/MEDLINE searches covering January 2014 to September 10, 2026 were complemented by citation chasing and selected landmark mechanistic articles. Sources were organized by evidence domain, study type and interpretive role, including pain chronification, neuroimmune and glial mechanisms, brain-network mechanisms, CBT outcomes, psychoneuroimmune pathways, perioperative prevention hypotheses, risk phenotyping and scalable delivery. No quantitative pooling or formal systematic/scoping-review workflow was performed. Experimental and translational studies support neuroimmune contributions to central sensitization and pain maintenance, whereas human evidence for direct CBT effects on microglial or astrocytic activation remains insufficient. CBT produces reproducible, generally small effects on pain intensity and more consistent benefits for interference, disability, distress, coping, sleep and function. CBT should be presented as a clinically valuable component of multimodal care and as a testable psychoneuroimmune hypothesis, not as a proven preventive, glial-targeting or disease-modifying treatment. Risk-stratified, early, component-specific and mechanism-embedded trials are needed before prevention claims are made.

papers.title: Unpacking the Obesity Paradox in Lung Cancer: A Nationwide Analysis of In-Hospital Mortality From the US National Inpatient Sample (2020-2022).
papers.abstract: Background Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Although obesity is an established risk factor for multiple malignancies, numerous studies have reported an "obesity paradox," wherein patients with obesity demonstrate improved survival compared with normal-weight or underweight individuals. Whether this survival advantage reflects a true protective biological mechanism or methodological artifacts such as reverse causation driven by cancer cachexia and selection bias remains controversial, particularly within the acute inpatient setting. We evaluated the independent association between documented obesity and in-hospital mortality among lung cancer hospitalizations. Methods We performed a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the US National Inpatient Sample (2020-2022). Adult hospitalizations (age ≥18 years) with a diagnosis of lung cancer were identified and dichotomized by the presence or absence of an International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) obesity code; the unit of analysis was the hospitalization rather than the individual patient, and the exposure was documented obesity coding rather than measured adiposity. Baseline demographics, comorbidities, and in-hospital complications were compared using the chi-squared test (categorical variables) and the Mann-Whitney U test (continuous variables). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and hospital-level covariates. Results Of 61,963 unweighted lung cancer hospitalizations, 7,065 (11.4%) carried an obesity code. Obese patients were younger (median: 68 vs. 70 years) and more often female (4,090/7,065 (57.9%) vs. 28,011/54,898 (51%)). They had a higher prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea (1,703 (24.1%) vs. 2,910 (5.3%)) but a lower weighted Elixhauser score (median: 10 vs. 16). In-hospital mortality was lower in the obese group (278 (3.9%) vs. 3,746 (6.8%); p<0.001). After adjustment, an obesity code was independently associated with 33% lower odds of in-hospital death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 0.67; 95% CI: 0.58-0.77; p<0.001). Conclusions Documented obesity coding was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality among lung cancer hospitalizations. However, the low sensitivity of administrative obesity coding, a binary exposure that cannot separate normal-weight from cachectic patients, and the susceptibility of hospitalized cohorts to collider and reverse-causation bias mean this association should not be interpreted as a protective effect of adiposity. The paradox is most parsimoniously explained by confounding by illness severity rather than a therapeutic target, and the finding should be interpreted as an association involving documented obesity coding rather than an effect of adiposity itself.

papers.title: Polysomnographic Sleep in Idiopathic Nightmares: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: This study conducted a systematic evaluation of polysomnographic differences between individuals with nightmares and healthy controls. Electronic searches of All EBM databases, EMBASE, Web of Science, and MEDLINE identified 14 eligible case-control studies; seven studies involving 112 individuals with nightmares and 112 controls were included in meta-analysis. The meta-analysis of sleep macro-architecture (such as total sleep time, wake after sleep onset, and sleep stage percentages) revealed no significant differences between individuals with nightmares and healthy controls. Furthermore, the limited available data regarding sleep micro-architecture (cyclic alternating patterns (CAP) and power spectral analysis (PSA)) and autonomic measures (heart rate and heart rate variability) in studies not subjected to meta-analysis makes it difficult to draw confident conclusions. Our meta-analysis revealed no significant differences in sleep macro-architecture. This finding highlights the importance of investigating sleep micro-architecture (such as CAP and PSA), which may be relevant to the physiology of nightmares. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and validated in future studies because of the limited available data.

papers.title: Type 2 Inflammation in Asthma and COPD: Biomarkers, Clinical Applications, and Targeted Therapies.
papers.abstract: Type 2 (T2) inflammation is a major pathogenic pathway in asthma and a clinically relevant endotype in a subgroup of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). This narrative review compares the mechanisms, biomarker-based assessment, and targeted treatment of T2 inflammation across these diseases. We focus on blood and sputum eosinophils, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), and total and allergen-specific immunoglobulin E (IgE), while examining discordance among biomarkers and the effects of corticosteroids, smoking, infection, circadian variation, coexisting T2 diseases, and population- or assay-dependent thresholds. We distinguish the adjunctive role of biomarkers in diagnosis from their more established roles in phenotyping, risk stratification, and treatment selection. Evidence from pivotal trials is synthesized for established and recently approved therapies, including the jurisdiction-specific positioning of depemokimab in severe asthma and mepolizumab in eosinophilic COPD, while investigational strategies targeting epithelial alarmins and related pathways are critically appraised. We also discuss clinical remission as an evolving treatment goal. Overall, repeated multidimensional assessment integrating biomarkers with clinical characteristics, lung function, comorbidities, exacerbation history, and treatment exposure is more informative than any single threshold and may support more precise management of asthma and COPD.

papers.title: Network Analysis of Symptom-Level Interrelationships Between Adverse Childhood Experiences and Insomnia Symptoms in Adolescents: A Large-Sample Study.
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for the physical and mental health of adolescents. Previous international studies have indicated a strong association between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and insomnia, although relevant reports focusing on Chinese adolescents remain limited. This online cross-sectional study ultimately included 6670 adolescents aged 12-18 years. Childhood adversity and insomnia symptoms were assessed using the Adverse Childhood Experiences Questionnaire and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), respectively. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests to compare ACE prevalence between groups, binary logistic regression to identify risk factors for insomnia symptoms, and Network analysis explored interrelationships among specific ACEs and insomnia symptoms, using centrality indices (strength, closeness, betweenness) to evaluate symptom influence. The prevalence of ACEs was 47.6% and insomnia symptoms was 20.6%. ACEs showed a cumulative dose-effect relationship with insomnia. Adolescents with ACEs had a significantly higher incidence of insomnia than those without. Physical abuse (OR = 1.41), emotional neglect (OR = 1.32), social isolation or exclusion (OR = 2.52), and witnessing community violence (OR = 1.57) were identified as significant risk factors for insomnia symptoms. Network analysis showed that ACE10 (family crime, strength z = 2.084) and ACE12 (Isolated or excluded, betweenness z = 3.594) were the most central ACE nodes. The strongest cross-domain connections were ISI4 (sleep dissatisfaction) and ACE12 (edge weights = 0.081), and between ISI1 (difficulty falling asleep) and ACE12 (edge weights = 0.077). ACEs and insomnia symptoms are prevalent and closely interrelated among Chinese adolescents. These findings highlight the need to strengthen the assessment of ACEs in this population and implement timely interventions to reduce the incidence of insomnia. However, as this is a cross-sectional study from a single province, further research is needed in terms of its generalizability.

papers.title: Diabetes Insipidus as a Rare Complication of Metastatic Breast Cancer With Pituitary Metastases.
papers.abstract: Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a rare but significant and life-threatening complication of metastatic breast cancer, typically arising when cancer spreads to the pituitary gland. This condition results from impaired secretion or action of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or arginine vasopressin (AVP), leading to symptoms including excessive urination and thirst. The posterior lobe of the pituitary and the infundibulum are most susceptible to metastatic involvement due to their direct arterial blood supply, making them more accessible to circulating tumor cells. This phenomenon explains why DI can be a manifestation of pituitary metastases. We report the case of a patient who presented with a five-week history of projectile vomiting, dizziness, blurred vision, headache, insatiable thirst, and nocturia. She reported urinating up to 12 times at night such that she struggled to sleep and would end up having daytime lethargy and fatigue. Biochemical evaluation demonstrated hyperosmolar serum, low urine osmolality, and low urine sodium, consistent with central DI. MRI revealed a pituitary stalk and suprasellar metastases with multiple new cerebral and cerebellar lesions. The patient underwent a desmopressin challenge leading to rapid improvement in polyuria and an increase in urine osmolality. Desmopressin confirmed an intact renal response, establishing the diagnosis of cranial DI secondary to pituitary metastases. Despite symptomatic benefit, her overall condition deteriorated due to progressive intracranial and systemic disease. She subsequently received whole-brain radiotherapy and palliative care but died three months after the diagnosis of DI. This case highlights central DI as a rare but clinically important manifestation of pituitary metastases in metastatic breast cancer. Prompt recognition and endocrine replacement, particularly with desmopressin, can provide meaningful symptomatic relief even when prognosis remains poor. Early multidisciplinary involvement, including endocrinology, oncology, radiology, and palliative care, is essential for optimizing quality of life in such complex cases.

papers.title: Repetitive negative thinking is associated with conflict-related neural activity that modulates evidence accumulation.
papers.abstract: Repetitive negative thinking (RNT), including worry and rumination, is a transdiagnostic feature of anxiety and depressive disorders and is linked to altered cognitive control. However, the decision-level mechanisms underlying these alterations are not well understood. Here, we examined whether individual variation in RNT is associated with neural and computational markers of conflict processing. Thirty-seven participants completed a flanker task while undergoing electroencephalography, and inhibitory control dynamics were quantified using hierarchical drift diffusion modeling. Behaviorally, RNT was not associated with traditional behavioral markers of conflict processing. At the neural level, higher RNT was associated with a more negative midfrontal conflict N2. Computationally, higher RNT was associated with larger congruent-incongruent differences in drift rate. Similarly, more negative midfrontal N2 activity was associated with greater modulation of drift rate congruency effects. An exploratory mediation analysis indicated that the midfrontal conflict N2 significantly mediated the effect of RNT on drift rate differences between congruent and incongruent trials. These findings indicate that elevated RNT is associated with heightened conflict-related neural activity that increases the degree to which evidence accumulation is modulated by conflict, suggesting a more reactive and context-sensitive engagement of cognitive control.
papers.journal: Journal of mood and anxiety disorders

papers.title: The Serial Mediating Roles of Repetitive Negative Thinking and Future Anxiety Between AI Competence Anxiety and Sleep Disturbance.
papers.abstract: Although artificial intelligence technologies are rapidly becoming widespread, the potential psychological risks associated with these technologies have not yet been sufficiently understood. Considering the expanding areas of use of artificial intelligence tools, examining the potential risk factors that may emerge from these technologies is considered important. Accordingly, the present study investigated the serial mediating roles of repetitive negative thinking (RNT) and future anxiety in the relationship between artificial intelligence competence anxiety and sleep disturbance. The study sample consisted of 364 individuals between the ages of 18 and 60 (71.98% female; Mage = 28.43, SD = 8.39). A two-step Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) approach was adopted in the analyses, and indirect effects were tested using the bootstrap method. In addition, gender, age, and frequency of artificial intelligence tool usage were included in the model as control variables. The results indicated significant indirect associations between artificial intelligence competence anxiety and sleep disturbance through RNT and future anxiety. Considering these variables together contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of the psychological mechanisms underlying the relationship between artificial intelligence competence anxiety and sleep disturbance. In this context, the findings contribute to the development of intervention and prevention programs aimed at reducing sleep disturbance and provide a guiding framework for practitioners.

papers.title: International Survey of Growth Hormone and Sleep Evaluation Practices in Infants With Prader-Willi Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Guidelines encourage polysomnogram (PSG) prior to starting growth hormone (GH) in individuals with Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS) to avoid adverse effects; however, this presents a challenge in infancy due to barriers regarding access and lack of normative data to guide recommendations. This international survey study assessed clinician practices regarding GH initiation and sleep evaluation in infants with PWS. The primary objective was to determine the prevalence of clinicians reporting they do not always perform a baseline PSG prior to GH Initiation and whether responses were associated with volume of PWS patients seen annually. A survey was distributed through 10 medical societies involved in PWS care. Respondents were grouped by volume of patients with PWS seen annually (<5 (low volume, LV), 5-20 (medium volume, MV), and >/= 21 (high volume, HV) and practice region (United States (US) vs. outside of the US). The primary outcome was evaluated using bivariate analysis, a test for trend, and multivariable logistic regression. All other outcome analyses were considered exploratory. We analysed 141 surveys from 18 countries (primarily US respondents; 79%). There were 58 (41%) LV, 42 (30%) MV, and 41 (29%) HV respondents. With respect to our primary outcome, HV respondents were more likely to answer "not always" when asked whether they perform baseline PSG prior to GH initiation with a decreasing trend to the LV group (HV: 56%, MV: 31%, LV: 26%, p = 0.003). Concurrently, the most common reason to forgo the baseline PSG in the US is to avoid delaying GH start (56%) and less concerns about side effects (apnea, sudden death) in this age group (54%). Outside of the US, the top reason was lack of availability of sleep lab (78%). In multivariable logistic regression, the odds of "not always" obtaining a baseline PSG prior to starting GH in infants was 3.66 times (95% CI: 1.48, 9.04) higher in individuals seeing more than 21 PWS patients (HV) compared to less than 5 (LV) when controlling for respondent's geographic location and years treating patients with PWS (p = 0.004). High volume PWS clinicians were more likely to report not always obtaining baseline PSG prior to starting GH in infants, primarily to prevent delayed therapy. These findings highlight a gap between guidelines and practice and support the need for prospective outcome data.

papers.title: EEG Signatures Support a Shrinking Spotlight of Attention After Errors.
papers.abstract: Errors inhibit attainment of our goals, but there are many ways to get back on track: from increased caution to heightened attention. In this report we examined EEG signatures of control and perception in 21 participants who completed a luminance-varying flanker task. Hierarchical Sequential Sample Modeling with a shrinking spotlight model was used for algorithmic decomposition of post-error adjustments. Control-related changes included a relationship between frontal midline theta power and raised decision threshold, as well as faster drift rate. Yet contrary to our hypothesis, these relationships were not significantly modulated following an error. Perceptual changes elicited by the luminance manipulation scaled with posterior alpha/beta power; both these extrinsic and intrinsic features loaded on an enhanced drift rate. Most importantly, after an error, this relationship between alpha/beta power and drift rate was enhanced. These findings support separate roles of neural systems in adaptive control: midfrontal regions were linked to generic control, whereas sensory-specific mechanisms of attentional adjustment were specifically recruited to boost evidence accumulation when control is needed.

papers.title: The Role of Lifestyle Medicine in Shaping and Supporting Successful Aging.
papers.abstract: Within gerontology, various theoretical perspectives on what it means to age successfully have emerged over recent decades (5) and garnered empirical support. Similarly, within medicine and related healthcare fields, research and practice have focused on healthy living in terms of physical health, mental health, and well-being. In recent years, the practice of Lifestyle Medicine (nutrition, physical activity, stress management, restorative sleep, social connection, and avoidance of risky substances) has emerged to describe the role of such lifestyle factors on health. The present article proposes a pathway to integrate lifestyle medicine with successful aging. We take a holistic approach to develop a model that merges the foundational pillars of lifestyle medicine with the principles of successful aging. This new approach to exploring the linkages between the principles of lifestyle medicine and the essential components of successful aging highlights how proactive behavioral health strategies related to nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress, and substances could play a role in fostering optimal aging in cognitive and physical functioning and disease prevention, thereby potentially yielding more positive outcomes for aging well.

papers.title: Distinct sleep and rest-activity profiles according to adjuvant treatment exposure in women treated for breast cancer.
papers.abstract: The associations between adjuvant treatment combinations and sleep-wake processes in women treated for breast cancer remain poorly understood, thereby limiting the development of individualized supportive care. This exploratory study aims to investigate this effect in women treated for breast cancer receiving chemotherapy (CT) combined or not with radio- (RT) and endocrine (ET) therapies on sleep-wake processes and cancer-related fatigue. Sixty-two participants were evaluated (21 patients receiving CT+RT+ET [CT group], 23 patients receiving RT+ET only [nonCT group], and 16 healthy control women [HC group]). Participants completed questionnaires assessing cancer-related fatigue and sleep complaints and wore a wrist actigraph for 72 hours to extract sleep-derived and rest-activity rhythm parameters. GLM served to compare groups when controlling for age and cancer stage. Correlation matrices were computed using Spearman's correlations to evaluate the links between variables in each patient' group. Sleep complaints and cancer-related fatigue did not significantly differ between groups. The CT group had fewer but longer nocturnal awakenings and shorter sleep-onset latency compared to both nonCT and HC groups. The nonCT group had lower dichotomy index-reflecting robustness of the rest-activity rhythm-than the CT group but did not differ significantly from the HCs. Fatigue was negatively correlated with rest-activity rhythm amplitude in the nonCT group. This exploratory study suggests that distinct patterns of sleep-wake parameters may be observed across the treatment exposure- groups (i.e., RT and ET + or - CT). These results should not be interpreted as evidence that treatment exposure itself explains the observed sleep-wake differences and require further investigation to be confirmed. This study was registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04391543.
